A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same manifold memorization hypothesis study. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the retained appendices A–E and identifying the added Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic diffusion experiments, CIFAR10 analyses using iDDPM and StyleGAN2-ADA, and Stable Diffusion memorization detection and mitigation results in Section 4 and appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally presents detailed human-labeled CIFAR10 image pairs in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The LID estimation procedures, differentiable memorization metrics, and attribution-guided GPT-4 prompt perturbations are retained. The clearer description of prompt-embedding optimization in Section 4.2 matches the procedure already documented in v1 Appendix D.3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the von Mises mixture, CIFAR10, LAION memorized images, LAION Aesthetics, COCO, and Tuxemon for the same detection and mitigation tasks. Appendix F expands reporting within the existing CIFAR10 evaluation.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: CFG norm in Figure 6, the attribution variants and uniform token selection in Figure 7, and random token addition in Figure 10. Renaming uniform selection from a baseline to an ablation does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: v1 Section 4.1 reports reviewing the top 250 candidates from each distance ranking for both CIFAR10 models. v2 Appendix F reports top 300 for iDDPM while retaining top 250 for StyleGAN2-ADA. Both generate 50,000 images per model. This is a limited reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a detailed qualitative examination of exact and reconstructive CIFAR10 memorization, separating labeled image pairs by model and retrieval metric in Figures 12–18. v1 showed selected examples in Figure 5a. The existing complexity-confounding analyses, mitigation ablation, and optimization failure examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repetitions per prompt in Section 4.2 and Appendix D.4. The statistical estimation and uncertainty-reporting practices are retained, with no added seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 12–18 add qualitative result entries, and Appendix F newly reports that no StyleGAN2-ADA pairs retrieved through calibrated L2 distance were labeled reconstructive. The existing quantitative plots and their reported trends are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, propositions, and proofs in Section 3 and appendices A and E are retained. The added Equation 16 in Appendix D.2 restates the existing CFG expression in the appendix notation; subsequent equation renumbering and notation edits do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about the MMH, overfitting-driven versus data-driven memorization, explanations of prior observations, and LID-based detection and mitigation. The additional exposition does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Section 2 adds explicit recommendations to address overfitting-driven memorization through more data or improved inductive biases. Appendix F explains combining retrieval metrics and using manual review through their differing retrieval results and reported false negatives. The existing limitations concerning complexity, mitigation performance, and discrete data remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F clarifies generated-to-training nearest-neighbor matching and labeling, states that candidate cutoffs were chosen by visual inspection, and supplies the labeled-pair record. Existing LID hyperparameters, prompt perturbation instructions, and the two codebase access links are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain the same. The Akbar et al. reference changes from its 2023 preprint to its 2025 publication. The expanded main-text discussion of distance-based definitions develops an argument already present in v1 Appendix A.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted language edits, expands the explanation of reconstructive memorization, revises the CIFAR10 protocol description, and adds Appendix F. The main section sequence and most prose remain stable; the header changes from preprint to ICLR 2025 publication status.

P2.justification: Appendix F adds seven image-pair galleries with captions organized by model, retrieval metric, and memorization type. Existing figures are retained, with localized changes including Figure 4 typography and placement and Figure 5 moving within its page.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's selected CIFAR10 examples and brief labeling description, v2 makes the classifications easier to inspect through the metric-separated galleries and cutoff-selection explanation in Appendix F. Targeted explanatory edits also improve clarity. These are limited gains in transparency and readability; the central theory and quantitative evidence remain essentially unchanged.
